name: Lake Burley Griffin
reason: Central lake with a 25 km path, cruises and waterfront sights; Visit Canberra and Wikivoyage list it (rule 1,2).
objection: Large and overlaps the institutions on its shore, but is the city's defining outing.

name: Lake Tuggeranong
reason: Only Wikivoyage's Tuggeranong pages (one family) name it: 'nice small walk around the lake', otherwise somewhere to sit. One source family, short visit.
objection: Case for: a named district lake with a walk. Against: an urban amenity lake, not a trip.

name: Lanyon Homestead
reason: Heritage homestead with guided tours, garden and cafe, open 10-4 except Mondays; Wikivoyage and Visit Canberra (rule 2).
objection: Closed Mondays, but a permanent museum venue.

name: Mount Franklin (Australian Capital Territory)
reason: Wikivoyage only mentions cross-country skiing there; the other counted source is the Namadgi tracks page on parks.act.gov.au (blocked, not read). Remote summit walk with Franklin Shelter.
objection: Case for: named summit walk with historic shelter. Against: remote, one thin source I could read, part of Namadgi National Park.

name: Mount Majura
reason: Wikivoyage names it as another important lookout in North Canberra reached by walking tracks, and ACT Parks has a reserve page. Separate peak from Mount Ainslie.
objection: Second-tier hill beside Ainslie; walkers only.

name: Mount Stromlo Observatory
reason: Observatory with public star nights and visitor facilities, named by Wikivoyage and Visit Canberra's 100 things (rule 2).
objection: Public access mostly by evening events and a cafe/visitor centre; still a permanent place.

name: Mugga-Mugga Cottage
reason: Wikivoyage lists a 1830s cottage open 10-2 on the first weekend of each month only, so it is not there whenever a visitor arrives (rule 4).
objection: Case for: three counted sources, genuine heritage house. Against: opens one weekend a month.

name: Mulligans Flat Woodland Sanctuary
reason: Fenced woodland sanctuary with trails and quolls; Wikivoyage, Visit Canberra and ACT Parks (rule 2).
objection: Sanctuary is a reserve; twilight tours are bookable but trails are open.

name: Namadgi National Park
reason: National park covering about 47% of the ACT with walks, huts and rock art; Wikivoyage has its own page and ACT Parks lists it.
objection: Huge; individual walks may be candidates separately.

name: National Arboretum Canberra
reason: Six counted sources incl. Wikivoyage with Dairy Farmers Hill lookout and Visit Canberra (rule 2).
objection: The lookout inside is part of this one.

name: National Archives of Australia
reason: National institution with two permanent public exhibitions in the Kings Avenue building (Wikivoyage).
objection: Archive-focused, lower draw than the galleries.

name: National Carillon
reason: Named by Wikivoyage and Visit Canberra, with recitals; landmark on the lake island.
objection: Exterior and sound mainly; short visit.

name: National Dinosaur Museum
reason: Museum with replicas and fossils in Nicholls; four counted sources incl. Wikivoyage and Visit Canberra (rule 2).
objection: Private family attraction, closed some days.

name: National Film and Sound Archive
reason: National institution with exhibitions and the Arc cinema; Visit Canberra museums page, Wikivoyage Acton (run rule: national institutions kept).
objection: Only two sources and Wikivoyage just mentions it nearby the Shine Dome.

name: National Gallery of Australia
reason: National gallery with Blue Poles and the largest Indigenous art collection, plus sculpture garden; four counted sources.
objection: None serious.

name: National Multicultural Festival
reason: Annual February festival, not there whenever a visitor arrives (rule 4).
objection: A big draw in its week, but an event.

name: National Museum of Australia
reason: National museum with First Australians Gallery and building tours; four counted sources.
objection: None serious.

name: National Portrait Gallery
reason: National gallery of portraits in Parkes; Wikivoyage, Visit Canberra (rule 2).
objection: Smaller than the NGA but a national institution.

name: National Zoo and Aquarium
reason: Zoo and aquarium with animal experiences; five counted sources. A place with animals, not an operator-only product.
objection: Privately owned and ticketed; accommodation (Jamala) is separate and not judged.

name: Old Parliament House
reason: Former Parliament House now Museum of Australian Democracy; one place with that candidate (kept here, the other rejected as duplicate). Wikivoyage and Visit Canberra.
objection: None serious.

name: Parliament House
reason: Free tours, galleries and roof lawn; four counted sources.
objection: None serious.

name: Parliamentary Triangle
reason: Precinct that contains Parliament House, High Court, National Gallery, Archives and others already candidates here; overlaps (run rule). Wikivoyage names it as the heart of Canberra sightseeing.
objection: Case for: a guide frames it as one walk. Against: duplicates its member institutions.

name: Questacon
reason: Interactive science centre in Parkes; four counted sources (rule 2).
objection: Family-oriented, ticketed.

name: Royal Australian Mint
reason: Free visitor tours and coin-making viewing, Wikivoyage lists hours; four counted sources.
objection: None serious.

name: Royal Canberra Golf Club
reason: Private golf club, not open to visitors as an attraction (club rule).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it, but only as a club.

name: Royal Military College Golf Club
reason: Golf course inside the Royal Military College, a club/closed to the public (club rule).
objection: Listed by Wikivoyage, but nothing for a visitor to do.

name: Scrivener Dam
reason: Wikivoyage has a viewing platform off Lady Denman Drive at the dam that created the lake; a short stop beside the zoo, named in several listings but a quick look (rule 3).
objection: Case for: five counted sources and named by Wikivoyage. Against: a 10-minute roadside lookout beside the zoo.

name: Southside Farmers Market
reason: Weekly farmers market, not there whenever a visitor arrives (rule 4).
objection: May be popular but is a weekly event.

name: Stromlo Forest Park
reason: Mountain-bike and walking forest park, named by Wikivoyage as one of the largest MTB parks near a city, plus Visit Canberra cycling page (rule 2).
objection: Low views but a recreation destination with trails open to all.

name: Stromlo Running Festival
reason: Annual running event, not there whenever a visitor arrives (rule 4).
objection: The venue (Stromlo Forest Park) is judged separately.

name: Thai Food and Cultural Festival
reason: Annual September festival at an embassy (rule 4; embassies are not visitor places).
objection: Cultural interest only during the event.

name: Weston Park
reason: Wikivoyage and Visit Canberra's 100 things name it as a popular park with a small train, maze and picnics (rule 2).
objection: Local district park; kept because two guides single it out.
